narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the prose frame and introduces each speech.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God, presiding over the heavenly court and questioning Satan.

satan.name: Satan
satan.note: The accuser among the sons of God, who challenges Job's integrity.

job.name: Job
job.note: Upright man of Hus, father of ten grown children, stricken and lamenting.

messenger-1.name: First messenger
messenger-1.note: Servant who escaped the Sabean raid on the oxen and asses; breathless.

messenger-2.name: Second messenger
messenger-2.note: Servant who escaped the fire of God that burned the sheep; breathless.

messenger-3.name: Third messenger
messenger-3.note: Servant who escaped the Chaldean raid on the camels; breathless.

messenger-4.name: Fourth messenger
messenger-4.note: Servant who escaped the house that fell on Job's children; breathless.

1.t: There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job, and that man was simple and upright, and fearing God, and avoiding evil.

2.t: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

3.t: And his possession was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a family exceedingly great: and this man was great among all the people of the east.

4.t: And his sons went, and made a feast by houses, every one in his day. And sending, they called their three sisters, to eat and drink with them.

5.t: And when the days of their feasting were gone about, Job sent to them, and sanctified them: and rising up early, offered holocausts for every one of them. For he said:
Lest perhaps my sons have sinned, and have blessed God in their hearts.

6.t: Now on a certain day, when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, Satan also was present among them.

7.t: And the Lord said to him:
I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.

8.t: And the Lord said to him:
Hast thou considered my servant, Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a simple and upright man, and fearing God, and avoiding evil?

9.t: Doth Job fear God in vain?

10.t: Hast thou not made a fence for him, and his house, and all his substance round about, blessed the works of his hands, and his possession hath increased on the earth?

11.t: But stretch forth thy hand a little, and touch all that he hath, and see if he bless thee not to thy face.

12.t: Then the Lord said to Satan:
Behold, all that he hath is in thy hand: only put not forth thy hand upon his person.
And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.

13.t: Now upon a certain day, when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine, in the house of their eldest brother,

14.t: There came a messenger to Job, and said:
The oxen were ploughing, and the asses feeding beside them,

15.t: And the Sabeans rushed in, and took all away, and slew the servants with the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

16.t: And while he was yet speaking, another came, and said:
The fire of God fell from heaven, and striking the sheep and the servants, hath consumed them; and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

17.t: And while he also was yet speaking, there came another, and said:
The Chaldeans made three troops, and have fallen upon the camels, and taken them; moreover, they have slain the servants with the sword: and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

18.t: He was yet speaking, and behold another came in, and said:
Thy sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,

19.t: A violent wind came on a sudden from the side of the desert, and shook the four corners of the house, and it fell upon thy children, and they are dead: and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

20.t: Then Job rose up, and rent his garments, and having shaven his head, fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,

21.t: Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away: as it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord.

22.t: In all these things Job sinned not by his lips, nor spoke he any foolish thing against God.
